title: Passage and Provision
premise: Coral Okonkwo, a salvage diver indebted to the navy for her father's crimes, is sent to recover a black-box transmitter from a wrecked survey vessel in a river delta the military denies operating in. When the transmitter reveals a live distress signal from an expedition lost beyond the Kessel Range, Coral deserts her orders and joins a disgraced guide, Tomas Reyes, to cross the mountains before the glacier calving season seals the pass for eight months. Pursued by her navy handler, Lieutenant Vance, who wants the expedition's findings buried, Coral discovers the 'wreck' was scuttled to hide a mining operation that poisoned the river and erased a village. At the calving glacier's edge she must choose between destroying the evidence that could clear her father's name and broadcasting it to save the survivors; she chooses the survivors, sacrificing the proof, and the final transmission forces an inquiry that finally gives her an identity of her own.
about_author: Silas Joubert is a former merchant marine who spent a decade running supply runs along West African river systems before turning to fiction. He writes from a houseboat in Luanda, where he claims the best plots arrive with the rainy season.

chapters.title: The Wreck They Don't Name
chapters.summary: Coral dives a navy wreck in the delta, recovering a transmitter she's ordered never to open. POV Coral. Establishes her debt, her father's disgrace, and her talent for staying invisible. Emotional beat: quiet resentment beneath professional calm.

chapters.title: Salt in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Lieutenant Vance reminds Coral what her debt costs and offers freedom in exchange for one last job: escort a survey team upriver. POV Coral. She glimpses a second signal on the transmitter and hides it. Beat: temptation and self-betrayal.

chapters.title: Upstream, Downwind
chapters.summary: Coral joins the river convoy and meets guide Tomas Reyes, cashiered for losing an expedition years ago. POV Tomas. He reads her as navy, she reads him as a liability; mutual distrust sparks. Beat: wary recognition of a fellow survivor.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't on the Chart
chapters.summary: The convoy passes a riverbank village absent from every map; an old woman recognizes Coral's surname. POV Coral. First hint her father's crimes connect to this river. Beat: unease turning to dread.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: The survey team's radio goes silent at the range foothills. Vance orders the convoy to turn back; Coral secretly copies the transmitter's distress coordinates. POV Coral. Beat: the moment obedience dies.

chapters.title: Deserter's Dawn
chapters.summary: Coral slips camp before first light; Tomas, guessing her plan, follows and offers to guide her across the Kessel Range before the calving season opens and closes the pass. POV Tomas. Beat: two runaways choosing each other's company.

chapters.title: Vance's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vance discovers the theft and mobilizes a recovery team, concealing from superiors that the lost expedition found evidence of the navy's poisoned river. POV Vance. Beat: corruption rationalizing itself.

chapters.title: The Ascent of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Coral and Tomas climb the foothills, trading stories of their disgraced parents. She admits she opened the transmitter; he admits the lost expedition years ago was his fault. POV alternating. Beat: guilt becoming intimacy.

chapters.title: Cold Camp
chapters.summary: A storm strands them in a cave with dwindling fuel; Tomas's frostbitten hand worsens. Coral's diving-honed calm keeps them alive. POV Coral. Beat: love surfacing in the space between survival tasks.

chapters.title: The Pass Opens
chapters.summary: The glacier calves early, opening the route for days only. They cross the ice bridge as Vance's team reaches the far side of the range. POV Tomas. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by pursuit.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: On the far slope they find the survey team's camp, looted but not abandoned; a survivor, engineer Amara Diallo, emerges half-starved. POV Amara. She reveals the navy scuttled the survey vessel. Beat: horror confirming suspicion.

chapters.title: The Poisoned River
chapters.summary: Amara's data proves a mining operation poisoned the delta village and the navy buried it, framing divers like Coral's father. POV Amara. Coral realizes the debt was engineered. Beat: identity shattered and reforged in anger.

chapters.title: Three Against the Mountain
chapters.summary: The trio races the closing weather while Vance's team triangulates their transmitter. Tomas's hand fails; Coral must lead. POV Coral. Beat: reluctant leadership accepted.

chapters.title: The Relay Station
chapters.summary: They reach an abandoned colonial relay station with a working transmitter, but broadcasting will reveal their position to Vance too. POV Tomas. Beat: the trap inside the solution.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Vance's team takes the station; Amara is captured, and Vance offers Coral her father's full pardon for the data drives. POV Vance, then Coral. Beat: the offer that would buy back her name.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Name
chapters.summary: Alone with Vance, Coral learns he personally signed the order that ruined her father. POV Coral. Beat: hatred clarifying into resolve; she pretends to accept.

chapters.title: The Calving
chapters.summary: Coral sabotages Vance's radio during the night, and the glacier calves catastrophically, destroying the station and separating both teams. POV Coral. Beat: chaos as liberation; Tomas missing.

chapters.title: White Silence
chapters.summary: Coral searches the icefield for Tomas through a whiteout, carrying the drives, half-frozen. POV Coral. Beat: grief and refusal; love against every practical argument.

chapters.title: The Long Descent
chapters.summary: She finds Tomas alive in a crevasse shelter; together they carry Amara's backup drive down the thawing river valley toward the delta village. POV Tomas. Beat: exhausted hope.

chapters.title: The Village Remembers
chapters.summary: In the unmapped village, the old woman and the survivors' testimony give Coral's evidence witnesses and a face. POV Amara. Beat: private truth becoming public record.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Using the wreck's own transmitter, Coral broadcasts the findings on an open channel; Vance's superiors, hearing everything, arrest him before he can silence it. POV Coral. Beat: climax — the invisible woman making herself heard.

chapters.title: Passage and Provision
chapters.summary: Months later, the inquiry clears her father and pardons her desertion; Coral declines the navy's offer and signs on to Tomas's rebuilt guide outfit, diving the delta on her own terms. POV Coral. Beat: identity chosen, not assigned; love and work as one.
